Resolution hinges on the official daily maximum reported by stations such as Central Park or LaGuardia, which integrate these mesoscale influences.

Updated short-range runs later today will clarify whether any brief clear spells allow a higher reading.

**Persistent cloud cover, widespread showers, and southwesterly flow are keeping daytime highs in Amsterdam tightly clustered around 21–23°C for August 29.** Official and model guidance from sources including GFS, ECMWF-influenced outlooks, and local services consistently point to a maximum near 22°C, with brief afternoon breaks in the rain allowing limited warming under mostly overcast skies and winds of 15–25 mph (roughly 7–11 m/s). This maritime air mass suppresses stronger heating compared with clearer late-August climatology.

Recent model runs have shown little shift in the expected peak, reinforcing trader consensus around the 22°C and 23°C contracts (52.5% and 34.5% implied probability). Lower-probability outcomes outside this narrow band reflect the low likelihood of either significant clearing for extra insolation or stronger cooling from heavier rain bands. The market-implied distribution therefore closely tracks the narrow forecast spread and typical model agreement on this short-range, high-confidence period.

**Forecasts from the National Weather Service and other models point to a high in the mid-to-upper 60s for San Francisco on August 29, 2026, consistent with the market's tight clustering around 66–69°F.** A reforming and deepening marine layer, combined with moderate-to-strong onshore northwest winds of 10–20 mph, is suppressing daytime heating by advecting cooler Pacific air inland. This typical summer pattern limits maximum temperatures well below the long-term average high of roughly 70°F for the date.

Recent model consensus shows partly cloudy skies with limited afternoon insolation and no significant warming aloft, keeping the outcome firmly in the 64–69°F range. The leading bins reflect minor uncertainties in exact marine-layer depth, wind gusts, and localized heating in less-exposed parts of the city. Higher outcomes (70°F+) would require a thinner layer or lighter winds, while lower readings depend on stronger onshore flow or more persistent cloud cover. Updated NWS guidance and afternoon model runs on August 28–29 will provide the clearest signals ahead of market resolution.

Lingering low-pressure moisture and southwesterly flow support convective activity that could cap temperatures near or below 34°C, while clearer intervals or reduced rainfall might allow peaks of 35–36°C. Global models such as GFS and ECMWF show modest spread in boundary-layer heating and cloud cover, creating the observed market distribution across 34–36°C outcomes. Traders weigh these variables against historical August maxima around 32–34°C and the narrow 48-hour window before resolution.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Recent forecasts indicate cloud cover and widespread rain or thunderstorms on August 30 will likely cap the daily maximum temperature in Guangzhou near 30–33 °C, aligning with the closely matched Polymarket probabilities centered on 31–33 °C.** 

Persistent moisture from the outer circulation of Typhoon Shadear (or a similar system) is expected to increase cloudiness and convective activity, reducing incoming solar radiation and evaporative cooling effects that otherwise drive peak afternoon temperatures in the region’s subtropical monsoon climate. Models show consensus on elevated humidity (70–90 %) and moderate winds, which further limit diurnal warming compared to the clearer, hotter conditions observed on August 28–29 (highs near 34–35 °C). 

Historical averages place the August 30 normal high at ~33 °C, but the current pattern of enhanced precipitation favors values toward the lower end of that range. Forecast uncertainty stems mainly from the exact timing and intensity of rain bands, which could allow brief clearing and a 33 °C reading or sustain overcast skies supporting only 31 °C. Updated model runs and official Guangdong Meteorological Bureau guidance in the next 24–48 hours will refine these thresholds ahead of market resolution.
